svg.text: Run charts: hear what data says

g.text: SHIFT = 6+ ONE SIDE
median line crossed?
something CHANGED!
TREND = 5+ CLIMBING
steady rise/fall =
drift, act early!
RUNS = TOO FEW
crossings = hidden
pattern, dig deeper!
ANNOTATE!
"PDSA 2 started →"
marks cause on chart!
READING RULE: plot median, watch for shifts (6+ one side), trends (5+ climbing), runs
(too few crossings) — then ANNOTATE changes ("new triage →"). No rules broken = common
variation, don't overreact; rules broken = investigate + act. Monthly dots minimum!
DASHBOARD DISCIPLINE: pick 5–7 ward metrics (falls, pressure injuries, hand-hygiene %,
discharge before noon, med errors, satisfaction) → traffic-light them → review MONTHLY as a
team → ONE action per red. Dashboards nobody reads are wallpaper.
PDSA + DATA: Plan (run chart baseline!) → Do (small test) → Study (chart moved?) → Act
(adopt/adapt/abandon). "We trained everyone" without a chart is hope, not improvement
(PRO-II M4!). QI without measures = motion without movement.
DHIMS2 LOOP: your tallies → district tables → YOUR facility review: coverage falling?
defaulters rising? stock-outs patterned? Bring the printout to staff meetings — data you
collected should change care you give (NUT records-into-action!).
PRESENTING DATA: one message per slide, big annotated charts, plain words ("falls halved
since night rounding — 8 to 4"), no 3D pies, no table walls. Tell the STORY the chart tells.
BENCHMARK HONESTLY: compare like-with-like (district hospitals vs peers, not teaching
hospitals!) — and celebrate publicly, investigate privately. Data shames nobody; hides nothing.
LINKS: PRO-II M4 QI engine · NUT M6 records · GER M7 audits.
MANTRA: "plot it, read it, act it, share it — data that rests, rots."
